history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. It's completely dead as far as the network goes.

I can help you troubleshoot this issue. First, I need to identify your account to check for any line or account-related problems. Could you please provide your phone number, customer ID, or your full name and date of birth?
My name is Sofia Martinez and my phone number is +1-617-555-0148.

Your line is currently suspended, which is why you have no service and cannot send picture messages. However, your recent bills are already paid, so the suspension is not due to an overdue bill.

I can help you resume your line so you can regain service. Once the suspension is lifted, you will need to reboot your device to restore connectivity. Would you like me to proceed with resuming your line now?
Yes, please go ahead and resume my line.

Your line has been resumed and is now active. Please reboot your device to restore your service. After restarting, you should be able to make calls, use data, and send picture messages again.

If you still experience any issues after rebooting, let me know and I can help you further troubleshoot.

history.content: I've rebooted my device as you asked, but I still have no service—there are no bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for letting me know. Since your line is now active but you still have no service, let's troubleshoot your device further.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know if you see any of the following:
- Airplane mode icon
- SIM card error or missing SIM message
- Signal bars (even if empty or with an “x”)
- Any other unusual icons

This information will help me determine the next steps to restore your service.
Actually, I do see the airplane mode icon in the status bar, along with 'No Signal' and 'Data Disabled.'

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your device, which disables all wireless connections, including cellular service. To restore your service, please turn off Airplane Mode.

Once you have turned off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars return and if you can use your phone normally. Let me know if you still have issues after disabling Airplane Mode.
Airplane mode is now off, but I still don't have any signal—there are still no bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. Since you still have no signal, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Sometimes, the SIM card may not be properly seated, which can cause a complete loss of service.

Please check your SIM card status on your device. If it shows as missing or not detected, try removing and reinserting your SIM card (reseating it). After doing this, let me know if your service returns or if you see any changes in the status bar.
I've removed and reinserted the SIM card. The SIM status now shows as active, but I still don't have any signal—there are no bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for reseating your SIM card and confirming its status is now active. Since you still have no signal, let's check your network mode settings. Sometimes, if your phone is set to use an older network type (like 2G or 3G), it may not connect properly.

Please check your phone’s network mode preference. If it is set to 2G or 3G, change it to “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only.” After making this change, see if your signal returns.

Let me know what your current network mode is set to, or if you need help changing this setting.
My network mode is already set to 4G/5G preferred, but I still have no signal or service.
YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
